candidate.why: 6 sites ran the identical headline; WorldMonitor counts them as 1 publisher (thin-grounding).

script: Here is a headline that ran yesterday: "Trump Announces Diesel Deal With Russia." WorldMonitor found it on six different radio station websites. KFBK. KOGO. KFYR. WLTP. WJNO. Big WAAX. Six mastheads. Six web addresses. The same words, word for word. WorldMonitor traces them back, and counts one publisher: iHeart, publishing one piece of copy. Six headlines. One source. Now, the diesel deal itself is real. The BBC, the Financial Times, CNBC and NBC each reported it on their own. That is what corroboration looks like. Six stations repeating one script is not. A headline in six places with one source is still one source.
